correctness.rationale: For a binary linear word with N=n−1 adjacent pairs, the transition counts obey c_01−c_10 in {-1,0,1}; every nonnegative count tuple with this difference, total N and the zero-transition connectivity exception is realized by runs. Exact counting of balanced and two imbalanced sectors gives Q_(2m)=3m²−m+2 and Q_(2m+1)=3m²+2m+2. Run-composition formulas give singleton profiles exactly for constant/one-transition words and two alternating even-length words. The proof has correct all-n quantifiers for n≥2; independent word-by-word enumeration for EVERY binary n=2,...,16 verified profile counts and singleton classifications, with a separate finite arithmetic spot-check through n=200 in the inspected verifier. Finite checks corroborate rather than replace the all-n run proof.
residual_risks: This is exact for binary linear read-length-two multispectra, not cyclic, larger alphabets, or larger read lengths.

value.rationale: The shortest nontrivial read length for binary string reconstruction is L=2. The exact achievable multispectrum count is quadratic rather than the standard cubic unconstrained profile bound, and the theorem classifies all uniquely reconstructible words at every length. This is a natural all-n exact invariant with a reproducible run characterization and useful benchmark for general reconstruction-code theory.
residual_risks: Does not determine optimal efficient representative encoding or noisy higher-read analogues.

limitations: Alphabet exactly {0,1}, length n≥2, adjacent linear length-two multispectra with multiplicities.
